doc_name: Molar ionization energies of the elements
text: These tables provide values for molar ionization energies expressed in kJ⋅mol−1, representing the energy required per mole to remove an electron from gaseous atoms or atomic ions. The first molar ionization energy corresponds to the removal of an electron from neutral atoms, while subsequent energies—such as the second, third, and so on—relate to the removal of electrons from singly, doubly, or higher charged ions. For ionization energies given in electron volts (eV), refer to the Ionization energies of the elements (data page). It should be noted that all data for elements starting with rutherfordium and beyond is predicted.
